assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimentally established, in physical terms, how electrons tunnel over long distances through protein matrices, with distance and driving-force dependence measured in ruthenium-modified proteins and linked to Marcus theory. This underlies respiratory and photosynthetic electron-transfer chains and is exactly the kind of fundamental mechanism in living systems that I weight most heavily.
assessment.attribution: Gray and Winkler are the clear experimental leaders of the protein tunnelling-pathway and hopping work. Others (Beratan, Onuchic, Dutton, Moser) contributed theory and natural-system tests, so a two-person prize leaves out some significant contributors.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation; the picture is stable and textbook. Recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Dutton, Moser, Beratan and Onuchic are not on the credited list, so priority questions on pathway theory and natural systems remain.
Marcus theory itself was already recognised, which may make the committee view this as an extension.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer is central to cytochrome c oxidase, photosystem II and many catalysts. The combination of concerted-mechanism concepts, thermochemical frameworks and theory has made proton and electron motion a quantitative physical-chemical topic. It is highly relevant to bioenergetics, and the principle is general.
assessment.attribution: Meyer introduced early PCET concepts, Mayer developed the thermochemical bond-weakening framework and concerted-proton-electron-transfer experiments, and Hammes-Schiffer supplied the theory. Nocera's PCET work is closely tied to artificial photosynthesis and could reasonably replace one of these names.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely adopted across enzymology, inorganic chemistry and electrocatalysis, though the field has no single decisive discovery event.
uncertainties: The candidacy rests on a line of work rather than one clearly attributable discovery.
Which three of four credited names is a close call and priority is distributed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structures of the Mo-nitrogenase FeMo cofactor, including the interstitial carbide and the CO and N2-surrogate complexes, together with mechanistic work on electron and proton delivery, address how a biological catalyst breaks the N2 triple bond. This is a deep problem in biological chemistry that combines structure with kinetics.
assessment.attribution: Rees led the key crystal structures and cofactor-binding studies, Einsle the high-resolution structure and identification of the central light atom, and Seefeldt the kinetic and spectroscopic mechanism. Dean and Ribbe were also major contributors, so three names omit others.
assessment.maturity: Structures are solid and independently reproduced, but the catalytic mechanism for N2 reduction is still debated, which makes the recognised discovery partly the structure and partly the mechanism.
uncertainties: The N2 reduction mechanism remains unresolved.
Allocation among Rees, Einsle, Dean, Seefeldt and Ribbe is contentious.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multidimensional heteronuclear NMR, isotope-labelling strategies and relaxation-dispersion methods made atomic-resolution structures and dynamics of proteins in solution routine, including invisible excited states and large complexes. It resembles the methods whose impact on structural and mechanistic biology was transformative.
assessment.attribution: Bax, Kay and Clore are the leading figures for the modern triple-resonance, TROSY-era and dynamics toolkit. Wuthrich was already recognised for the foundations; Wagner and Palmer also contributed, so some credit is shared.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with decades of widespread use. The risk is the committee viewing it as incremental on an already-awarded NMR prize.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier NMR recognition may weigh against it.
Method development spans many groups and clean attribution of a single decisive invention is hard.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers made diffraction-before-destruction possible for micro- and nanocrystals, enabling room-temperature structures and time-resolved structural movies of reacting proteins. This visualises dynamic biochemical processes in three dimensions, which I value highly.
assessment.attribution: Hajdu proposed the diffraction-before-destruction concept, Chapman led the first demonstrations and methods, and Fromme drove the membrane-protein nanocrystal work. Schlichting's time-resolved work is also prominent, so the configuration is arguable.
assessment.maturity: The method is confirmed at several facilities, but the number of transformative biochemical results is still growing and the facilities are young, so timing may be early.
uncertainties: Maturity of mechanistic results is still developing.
Credit between concept, method and early applications is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The funnelled energy-landscape view resolved the Levinthal paradox and gave protein folding a physical framework, which experiments on folding kinetics and phi-value analysis then tested. It has changed how structure, dynamics and function are discussed in biophysical chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic are principal theorists of the landscape and funnel concepts; Fersht provided the experimental mapping. Dill and Bryngelson made important parallel contributions, so priority is diffuse.
assessment.maturity: Mature and heavily cited, but largely conceptual, and the practical impact was overtaken by structure prediction.
uncertainties: Credit is distributed among many theorists.
The committee may regard it as a theoretical framework more than a discrete discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as a principle organising cellular biochemistry has reframed thinking about membraneless compartments. It joins physical chemistry of polymers to cell biology and has had broad impact.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne showed P granules behave as liquids; Rosen showed multivalent-interaction phase behaviour in vitro. Pappu and Mittag provide the physical-chemical basis, so the three-person limit is a real constraint.
assessment.maturity: Fast-growing but with ongoing debate about physiological relevance and what counts as true phase separation in cells, which suggests it may be premature.
uncertainties: Physiological significance and mechanism are contested.
Several important contributors fall outside three names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mass-spectrometry proteomics, including shotgun and quantitative methods, made it possible to identify and quantify thousands of proteins and modifications. It is a methodological enabler used across biochemistry, although the contribution is a technology platform rather than a single mechanism.
assessment.attribution: Mann, Aebersold and Yates are the most commonly central figures. Hunt, Gygi and Heck are also significant, and since earlier MS prizes already covered ionisation, some credit overlap exists.
assessment.maturity: The methods are mature and widely validated.
uncertainties: It is a line of work and attribution among Mann, Aebersold, Yates, Hunt and Gygi is not clean.
